1:1.en: Moses received Torah from Sinai and handed it down to Joshua; Joshua to the elders; the elders to the prophets; and the prophets handed it down to the members of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment; raise up many disciples; and make a fence for the Torah.

1:10.en: Shemaiah and Avtalyon received from them. Shemaiah says: Love work, hate lordship, and do not make yourself known to the ruling power.

1:11.en: Avtalyon says: Sages, be careful with your words, lest you incur the liability of exile and be exiled to a place of evil waters, and the disciples who come after you drink and die, and so it turns out that the name of Heaven is profaned.

1:12.en: Hillel and Shammai received from them. Hillel says: Be of the disciples of Aaron, loving peace and pursuing peace, loving people and bringing them near to the Torah.

1:13.en: He used to say: One who spreads his name far loses his name; and one who does not add will cease; and one who does not learn deserves to die; and one who makes use of the crown passes away.

1:14.en: He used to say: If I am not for myself, who is for me? And when I am for myself, what am I? And if not now, when?

1:15.en: Shammai says: Make your Torah fixed. Say little and do much, and receive every person with a pleasant countenance.

1:16.en: Rabban Gamliel used to say: Make for yourself a teacher, and withdraw from doubt, and do not make a habit of tithing by estimates.

1:17.en: Shimon his son says: All my days I grew up among the sages, and I have found nothing good for the body except silence. And it is not expounding that is the main thing, but action. And whoever multiplies words brings sin.

1:18.en: Rabban Shimon son of Gamliel says: On three things the world stands: on justice, and on truth, and on peace, as it is said (Zechariah 8): Judge truth and a judgment of peace in your gates.

1:2.en: Shimon the Righteous was of the remnants of the Great Assembly. He used to say: On three things the world stands: on the Torah, and on the Temple service, and on acts of kindness.

1:3.en: Antigonos of Sokho received from Shimon the Righteous. He used to say: Do not be like servants who serve the master on condition of receiving a gratuity, but be like servants who serve the master not on condition of receiving a gratuity; and let the fear of Heaven be upon you.

1:4.en: Yose son of Yoezer of Tzereda and Yose son of Yochanan of Jerusalem received from them. Yose son of Yoezer of Tzereda says: Let your house be a meeting place for the sages; and be covered in the dust of their feet; and drink their words with thirst.

1:5.en: Yose son of Yochanan of Jerusalem says: Let your house be open wide; and let the poor be members of your household; and do not talk too much with the woman. They said this of one's own wife; how much more so of the wife of his fellow. From here the sages said: Whenever a man talks too much with the woman, he brings evil upon himself, and neglects words of Torah, and in the end inherits Gehinnom.

1:6.en: Yehoshua son of Perachya and Nittai the Arbelite received from them. Yehoshua son of Perachya says: Make for yourself a teacher; and acquire for yourself a friend; and judge every person favorably.

1:7.en: Nittai the Arbelite says: Keep far from a bad neighbor, and do not associate with a wicked person, and do not despair of retribution.

1:8.en: Judah son of Tabbai and Shimon son of Shetach received from them. Judah son of Tabbai says: Do not make yourself like those who arrange the pleas before the judges. When litigants stand before you, let them be in your eyes like the wicked; and when they depart from before you, let them be in your eyes like the innocent, once they have accepted the judgment upon themselves.

1:9.en: Shimon son of Shetach says: Be thorough in examining the witnesses, and be careful with your words, lest from them they learn to lie.

2:1.en: Rabbi says: Which is the upright path that a person should choose for himself? Whatever is a glory to those who do it and a glory to him from people. Be as careful with a light commandment as with a weighty one, for you do not know the reward given for the commandments. Reckon the loss from a commandment against its reward, and the gain from a transgression against its loss. Look at three things and you will not come to transgression: know what is above you: an eye that sees and an ear that hears, and all your deeds are written in a book.

2:10.en: They said three things. Rabbi Eliezer says: Let your fellow's honor be as dear to you as your own, and do not be quick to anger. And repent one day before your death. And warm yourself at the fire of the sages, and beware of their coals, lest you be burned; for their bite is the bite of a fox, their sting is the sting of a scorpion, their whisper is the whisper of a fiery serpent, and all their words are like coals of fire.

2:11.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says: The evil eye, the evil impulse, and hatred of people remove a person from the world.

2:12.en: Rabbi Yose says: Let your fellow's money be as dear to you as your own. Prepare yourself to learn Torah, for it is not an inheritance to you. And let all your deeds be for the sake of Heaven.

2:13.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Be careful in reciting the Shema and in the Prayer. And when you pray, do not make your prayer a fixed routine, but a plea for mercy and supplication before the Omnipresent, blessed be He, as it is said (Joel 2): “For He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger, abounding in kindness, and relenting of the evil.” And do not be wicked in your own eyes.

2:14.en: Rabbi Elazar says: Be diligent in learning Torah, and know what to answer an Epicurean. And know before whom you toil. And faithful is the master of your work to pay you the reward of your labor.

2:15.en: Rabbi Tarfon says: The day is short, the work is great, the laborers are lazy, the reward is abundant, and the master of the house is pressing.

2:16.en: He used to say: It is not for you to finish the work, and you are not free to desist from it. If you have learned much Torah, they give you much reward. And faithful is the master of your work to pay you the reward of your labor. And know that the granting of the reward of the righteous is in the world to come.

2:2.en: Rabban Gamliel, son of Rabbi Yehuda the Patriarch, says: Torah study is excellent together with a worldly occupation, for the toil of both makes sin forgotten. And any Torah study that has no work with it in the end comes to nothing and draws sin along. And all who labor with the community should labor with them for the sake of Heaven, for the merit of their fathers supports them and their righteousness stands forever. And you, I credit to you a great reward as if you had done it.

2:3.en: Be wary of the authorities, for they do not draw a person near except for their own needs. They appear as friends when it is to their benefit, and they do not stand by a person in his hour of need.

2:4.en: He used to say: Do His will as if it were your will, so that He will do your will as if it were His will. Set aside your will before His will, so that He will set aside the will of others before your will. Hillel says: Do not separate yourself from the community, and do not trust yourself until the day of your death, and do not judge your fellow until you reach his place, and do not say a thing that cannot be heard, for in the end it will be heard. And do not say, 'When I am free I will study': perhaps you will not be free.

2:5.en: He used to say: No boor fears sin, and no unlearned person is pious, and no shy person learns, and no short-tempered person teaches, and not everyone who does much business becomes wise. And in a place where there are no men, strive to be a man.

2:6.en: He also saw a skull floating on the surface of the water. He said to it: 'Because you drowned others, they drowned you, and in the end those who drowned you will be drowned.'

2:7.en: He used to say: The more flesh, the more worms. The more property, the more anxiety. The more wives, the more witchcraft. The more maidservants, the more lewdness. The more male slaves, the more robbery. The more Torah, the more life. The more sitting in study, the more wisdom. The more counsel, the more understanding. The more charity, the more peace. One who has acquired a good name has acquired it for himself. One who has acquired for himself words of Torah has acquired for himself the life of the world to come.

2:8.en: Rabban Yohanan son of Zakkai received from Hillel and from Shammai. He used to say: If you have learned much Torah, do not claim credit for yourself, for to this end you were created. Rabban Yohanan son of Zakkai had five disciples, and these are they: Rabbi Eliezer son of Hyrcanus, Rabbi Yehoshua son of Hananiah, Rabbi Yose the Priest, Rabbi Shimon son of Netanel, and Rabbi Elazar son of Arach. He used to enumerate their praises: Rabbi Eliezer son of Hyrcanus, a plastered cistern that does not lose a drop. Rabbi Yehoshua son of Hananiah, happy is she who bore him. Rabbi Yose the Priest, a pious man. Rabbi Shimon son of Netanel, a fearer of sin. And Rabbi Elazar son of Arach, a spring gathering strength. He used to say: If all the sages of Israel were in one pan of a scale, and Eliezer son of Hyrcanus in the other pan, he would outweigh them all. Abba Shaul says in his name: If all the sages of Israel were in one pan of a scale, and Rabbi Eliezer son of Hyrcanus also with them, and Rabbi Elazar son of Arach in the other pan, he would outweigh them all.

2:9.en: He said to them: Go out and see which is the right way that a person should cling to. Rabbi Eliezer says: A good eye. Rabbi Yehoshua says: A good companion. Rabbi Yose says: A good neighbor. Rabbi Shimon says: One who sees what is to come. Rabbi Elazar says: A good heart. He said to them: I prefer the words of Elazar son of Arach to your words, for your words are included in his words. He said to them: Go out and see which is the evil way that a person should keep far from. Rabbi Eliezer says: An evil eye. Rabbi Yehoshua says: An evil companion. Rabbi Yose says: An evil neighbor. Rabbi Shimon says: One who borrows and does not repay. One who borrows from a person is as one who borrows from the Omnipresent, blessed be He, as it is said (Psalms 37): The wicked one borrows and does not repay, but the Righteous One is gracious and gives. Rabbi Elazar says: An evil heart. He said to them: I prefer the words of Elazar son of Arach to your words, for your words are included in his words.

3:1.en: Akavya son of Mahalalel says: Consider three things and you will not come to the point of transgression. Know where you came from, and where you are going, and before whom you are destined to give account and reckoning. Where you came from: from a putrid drop. And where you are going: to a place of dust, maggot and worm. And before whom you are destined to give account and reckoning: before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.

3:10.en: He used to say: Anyone with whom the spirit of people is pleased, the spirit of the Omnipresent is pleased with him. And anyone with whom the spirit of people is not pleased, the spirit of the Omnipresent is not pleased with him. Rabbi Dosa son of Harkinas says: Morning sleep, midday wine, the chatter of children, and sitting in the synagogues of the unlearned remove a person from the world.

3:11.en: Rabbi Elazar of Modi'in says: One who profanes the sacred things, and one who despises the festivals, and one who shames his fellow in public, and one who breaks the covenant of Abraham our father, peace be upon him, and one who brazenly flouts the Torah, contrary to the halakha: even though he has Torah and good deeds, he has no share in the world to come.

3:12.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: Be yielding to a superior, and composed with the young, and receive every person with joy.

3:13.en: Rabbi Akiva says: Laughter and levity accustom a person to lewdness. The Masoretic tradition is a fence for the Torah; tithes are a fence for wealth; vows are a fence for abstinence; a fence for wisdom is silence.

3:14.en: He used to say: Beloved is a human being, for he was created in the image. Extra love was made known to him, that he was created in the image, as it is said (Genesis 9): 'For in the image of God He made the human being.' Beloved are Israel, for they were called children of the Omnipresent. Extra love was made known to them, that they were called children of the Omnipresent, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14): 'You are children of the LORD your God.' Beloved are Israel, for a desirable vessel was given to them. Extra love was made known to them, that a desirable vessel was given to them, by which the world was created, as it is said (Proverbs 4): 'For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake my Torah.'

3:15.en: Everything is foreseen, yet freedom of choice is given; the world is judged with goodness, and all is according to the abundance of deeds.

3:16.en: He used to say: Everything is given as a pledge, and a net is spread over all the living. The shop is open, the shopkeeper extends credit, the ledger is open, and the hand writes; and whoever wishes to borrow may come and borrow. The collectors make their rounds constantly, every day, and exact payment from a person with his knowledge and without his knowledge. They have what to rely on, and the judgment is a judgment of truth. And everything is prepared for the banquet.

3:17.en: Rabbi Elazar son of Azariah says: If there is no Torah, there is no proper conduct; if there is no proper conduct, there is no Torah. If there is no wisdom, there is no fear; if there is no fear, there is no wisdom. If there is no understanding, there is no knowledge; if there is no knowledge, there is no understanding. If there is no flour, there is no Torah; if there is no Torah, there is no flour. He used to say: Anyone whose wisdom exceeds his deeds, to what is he compared? To a tree whose branches are many and whose roots are few; and the wind comes and uproots it and overturns it on its face, as it is said (Jeremiah 17): 'He shall be like a bare shrub in the desert plain, and shall not see when good comes; he shall dwell in the parched places of the wilderness, a salt land, uninhabited.' But anyone whose deeds exceed his wisdom, to what is he compared? To a tree whose branches are few and whose roots are many, so that even if all the winds in the world come and blow against it, they do not move it from its place, as it is said (ibid.): 'He shall be like a tree planted by water, and by a stream it sends out its roots, and it shall not see when heat comes; its leaf shall be fresh, and in a year of drought it shall not worry, and it shall not cease from yielding fruit.'

3:18.en: Rabbi Eliezer son of Hisma says: Bird offerings and the openings of the menstruant, these very things are the essentials of the laws. Astronomical cycles and gematria are the desserts of wisdom.

3:2.en: Rabbi Hanina, the deputy of the priests, says: Pray for the welfare of the government, for were it not for the fear of it, each man would have swallowed his fellow alive. Rabbi Hanina son of Teradion says: Two who sit with no words of Torah between them, this is a seat of scoffers, as it is said (Psalm 1): "and in the seat of scoffers he has not sat." But two who sit with words of Torah between them, the Shekhinah dwells among them, as it is said (Malachi 3): "Then those who fear the LORD spoke, each man to his fellow, and the LORD listened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before him for those who fear the LORD and for those who esteem his name." I know this only of two. From where do we learn that even for one who sits and occupies himself with Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, sets a reward for him? As it is said (Lamentations 3): "He sits alone and murmurs, for he has taken it upon himself."

3:3.en: Rabbi Shimon says: Three who ate at one table and did not say words of Torah over it, it is as if they ate of sacrifices to the dead, as it is said (Isaiah 28): "For all the tables are full of vomit and filth, with no place." But three who ate at one table and said words of Torah over it, it is as if they ate from the table of the Omnipresent, blessed be He, as it is said (Ezekiel 41): "And he spoke to me: This is the table that is before the LORD."

3:4.en: Rabbi Hanina son of Hakhinai says: One who is awake at night, or who walks on the road alone, and who turns his heart to idleness: this one is answerable with his life.

3:5.en: Rabbi Nehunya son of Hakanah says: Whoever takes upon himself the yoke of Torah, they remove from him the yoke of the government and the yoke of worldly occupation. And whoever throws off from himself the yoke of Torah, they place upon him the yoke of the government and the yoke of worldly occupation.

3:6.en: Rabbi Halafta son of Dosa, of Kefar Hananiah, says: Ten who sit and occupy themselves with Torah, the Shekhinah dwells among them, as it is said (Psalm 82): "God stands in the congregation of God." And from where even five? As it is said (Amos 9): "and his bundle upon the earth he has founded." And from where even three? As it is said (Psalm 82): "In the midst of judges he judges." And from where even two? As it is said (Malachi 3): "Then those who fear the LORD spoke, each man to his fellow, and the LORD listened and heard, and so on." And from where even one? As it is said (Exodus 20): "In every place where I cause my name to be remembered I will come to you and bless you."

3:7.en: Rabbi Elazar of Bartota says: Give Him what is His, for you and what is yours are His. And so David says: “For everything comes from You, and from Your hand we have given to You.” Rabbi Shimon says: One who walks on the road and reviews his learning, and interrupts his learning and says, “How fine is this tree, and how fine is this furrow!”, Scripture accounts it to him as if he were forfeiting his life.

3:8.en: Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai, in the name of Rabbi Meir, says: Whoever forgets a single thing from his learning, Scripture accounts it to him as if he were forfeiting his life, as it is said: “Only take heed to yourself and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget the things that your eyes saw.” One might think this holds even if his learning was too hard for him; the teaching says: “and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life.” Thus he is not forfeiting his life until he sits and removes them from his heart.

3:9.en: Rabbi Hanina son of Dosa says: Anyone whose fear of sin comes before his wisdom, his wisdom endures. But anyone whose wisdom comes before his fear of sin, his wisdom does not endure. He used to say: Anyone whose deeds exceed his wisdom, his wisdom endures. But anyone whose wisdom exceeds his deeds, his wisdom does not endure.

4:1.en: Ben Zoma says: Who is wise? One who learns from every person, as it is said: "From all my teachers I have gained insight, for Your testimonies are my meditation." Who is mighty? One who subdues his impulse, as it is said: "Better is one slow to anger than a mighty man, and one who rules his spirit than one who captures a city." Who is rich? One who rejoices in his portion, as it is said: "When you eat the toil of your hands, happy are you, and it is well with you." "Happy are you": in this world. "And it is well with you": in the world to come. Who is honored? One who honors people, as it is said: "For those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me will be lightly esteemed."

4:10.en: Rabbi Meir says: Limit your business, and engage in the Torah. And be humble of spirit before every person. And if you neglect the Torah, you have many idle ones against you. And if you toil in the Torah, He has much reward to give you.

4:11.en: Rabbi Eliezer son of Jacob says: One who performs one commandment acquires for himself one advocate. And one who commits one transgression acquires for himself one accuser. Repentance and good deeds are like a shield before punishment. Rabbi Johanan the Sandal-maker says: Every assembly that is for the sake of Heaven will in the end endure. And one that is not for the sake of Heaven will not in the end endure.

4:12.en: Rabbi Eleazar son of Shammua says: Let the honor of your student be as dear to you as your own, and the honor of your colleague like the reverence for your teacher, and the reverence for your teacher like the reverence for Heaven.

4:13.en: Rabbi Yehuda says: Be careful in study, for an error in study counts as deliberate sin. Rabbi Shimon says: There are three crowns: the crown of Torah, the crown of priesthood, and the crown of kingship; but the crown of a good name rises above them.

4:14.en: Rabbi Nehorai says: Go into exile to a place of Torah, and do not say that it will come after you, that your colleagues will establish it in your hand. And do not lean on your own understanding.

4:15.en: Rabbi Yannai says: It is not in our hands: not the tranquility of the wicked, nor yet the suffering of the righteous. Rabbi Matya son of Harash says: Be first to greet every person, and be a tail to lions, and do not be a head to foxes.

4:16.en: Rabbi Yaakov says: This world is like a vestibule before the world to come. Prepare yourself in the vestibule, so that you may enter the great hall.

4:17.en: He used to say: Better is one hour of repentance and good deeds in this world than all the life of the world to come. And better is one hour of spiritual contentment in the world to come than all the life of this world.

4:18.en: Rabbi Shimon son of Elazar says: Do not appease your fellow at the time of his anger, and do not comfort him at the time when his dead lies before him, and do not question him at the time of his vow, and do not strive to see him at the time of his disgrace.

4:19.en: Samuel the Small says: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and when he stumbles, let your heart not be glad, lest the Lord see it, and it displease Him, and He turn His anger away from him.

4:2.en: Ben Azzai says: Run to a light commandment as to a weighty one, and flee from transgression. For a commandment draws a commandment, and a transgression draws a transgression. For the reward of a commandment is a commandment, and the reward of a transgression is a transgression.

4:20.en: Elisha son of Avuyah says: One who learns as a child, to what is he compared? To ink written on new paper. And one who learns as an old man, to what is he compared? To ink written on erased paper. Rabbi Yose son of Yehudah, a man of Kefar HaBavli, says: One who learns from the young, to what is he compared? To one who eats unripe grapes and drinks wine from its winepress. And one who learns from the old, to what is he compared? To one who eats ripe grapes and drinks aged wine. Rabbi says: Do not look at the jar, but at what is in it. There is a new jar full of old wine, and an old one in which there is not even new.

4:21.en: Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says: Envy, desire, and honor take a person out of the world.

4:22.en: He used to say: Those who are born are to die, and the dead are to be revived, and the living are to be judged; to know, to make known, and to come to know that He is God, He is the Former, He is the Creator, He is the Discerner, He is the Judge, He is the Witness, He is the Plaintiff, and He is destined to judge. Blessed is He, before whom there is no injustice, no forgetfulness, no partiality, and no taking of bribes, for everything is His. And know that everything is according to the reckoning. And do not let your impulse assure you that Sheol is a place of refuge for you, for against your will you were formed, and against your will you were born, and against your will you live, and against your will you die, and against your will you are destined to give judgment and account before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.

4:3.en: He used to say: Do not be contemptuous of any person, and do not dismiss any thing as remote; for there is no person who has no hour, and no thing that has no place.

4:4.en: Rabbi Levitas of Yavneh says: Be very, very humble of spirit, for the hope of man is the worm. Rabbi Yohanan son of Beroka says: Whoever profanes the name of Heaven in secret, payment is exacted from him in the open. Whether unwitting or willful, in profaning the Name.

4:5.en: Rabbi Ishmael, his son, says: One who learns Torah in order to teach, they enable him to learn and to teach. And one who learns in order to do, they enable him to learn and to teach, to keep and to do. Rabbi Zadok says: Do not make them a crown to exalt yourself with, nor a spade to dig with. And thus Hillel used to say: "And he who makes use of the crown passes away." Hence you have learned: whoever derives benefit from the words of Torah takes his life from the world.

4:6.en: Rabbi Yose says: Whoever honors the Torah, his body is honored by people. And whoever profanes the Torah, his body is profaned by people.

4:7.en: Rabbi Ishmael his son says: One who holds himself back from judging removes from himself enmity, robbery, and a vain oath. But one who is overbold of heart in giving rulings is a fool, wicked, and haughty of spirit.

4:8.en: He used to say: Do not judge alone, for none judges alone but One. And do not say, "Accept my opinion," for they are permitted, and you are not.

4:9.en: Rabbi Jonathan says: Whoever fulfills the Torah from poverty will in the end fulfill it from wealth. And whoever neglects the Torah from wealth will in the end neglect it from poverty.

5:1.en: By ten utterances the world was created. What does the text teach in saying so? Could it not have been created by a single utterance? Rather, it was to exact punishment from the wicked, who destroy the world that was created by ten utterances, and to give good reward to the righteous, who sustain the world that was created by ten utterances.

5:10.en: There are four dispositions among people. One who says, "What is mine is mine, and what is yours is yours": this is a middling disposition; and some say, this is the disposition of Sodom. "What is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine": an unlearned person. "What is mine is yours, and what is yours is yours": a pious person. "What is mine is mine, and what is yours is mine": a wicked person.

5:11.en: There are four dispositions in temperaments. Easy to anger and easy to appease: his gain is outweighed by his loss. Hard to anger and hard to appease: his loss is outweighed by his gain. Hard to anger and easy to appease: a pious person. Easy to anger and hard to appease: a wicked person.

5:12.en: There are four dispositions in disciples. Quick to hear and quick to forget: his gain is outweighed by his loss. Hard to hear and hard to forget: his loss is outweighed by his gain. Quick to hear and hard to forget: a wise person. Hard to hear and quick to forget: this is a bad lot.

5:13.en: There are four types in giving charity. One who wants to give but wants others not to give has an evil eye toward what belongs to others. One who wants others to give but himself not to give has an evil eye toward his own. One who wants to give and wants others to give is pious. One who wants neither himself nor others to give is wicked.

5:14.en: There are four types in going to the house of study. One who goes but does not do: the reward of going is in his hand. One who does but does not go: the reward of doing is in his hand. One who goes and does is pious. One who neither goes nor does is wicked.

5:15.en: There are four types among those who sit before the sages: a sponge, a funnel, a strainer, and a sieve. A sponge, because it absorbs everything. A funnel, because it takes in through this and lets out through that. A strainer, because it lets the wine out and retains the dregs. And a sieve, because it lets out the fine meal and retains the choice flour.

5:16.en: Any love that depends on a thing: when the thing ceases, the love ceases. And that which does not depend on a thing never ceases. Which is the love that depends on a thing? This is the love of Amnon and Tamar. And that which does not depend on a thing? This is the love of David and Jonathan.

5:17.en: Every dispute that is for the sake of Heaven will in the end endure. And one that is not for the sake of Heaven will not in the end endure. Which is a dispute that is for the sake of Heaven? This is the dispute of Hillel and Shammai. And one that is not for the sake of Heaven? This is the dispute of Korah and all his company.

5:18.en: Whoever makes the many meritorious, no sin comes through him. And whoever causes the many to sin, they do not give him the means to repent. Moses was meritorious and made the many meritorious; the merit of the many rests on him, as it is said, Deuteronomy 33: "He performed the righteousness of the LORD, and His judgments with Israel." Jeroboam sinned and caused the many to sin; the sin of the many rests on him, as it is said, 1 Kings 15: "For the sins of Jeroboam (son of Nebat), which he sinned and which he caused Israel to sin."

5:19.en: Whoever has these three things is of the disciples of Abraham our father; and three other things, of the disciples of Balaam the wicked. A good eye, a humble spirit, and a modest soul: of the disciples of Abraham our father. An evil eye, a haughty spirit, and a broad soul: of the disciples of Balaam the wicked. What is the difference between the disciples of Abraham our father and the disciples of Balaam the wicked? The disciples of Abraham our father eat in this world and inherit in the world to come, as it is said: "To bequeath to those who love me substance, and I will fill their treasuries." But the disciples of Balaam the wicked inherit Gehinnom and go down to the pit of destruction, as it is said: "And You, God, will bring them down to the pit of destruction; men of blood and deceit shall not live out half their days; but I will trust in You."

5:2.en: Ten generations from Adam to Noah, to make known how patient He is, for all the generations kept on provoking Him until He brought upon them the waters of the Flood. Ten generations from Noah to Abraham, to make known how patient He is, for all the generations kept on provoking Him until Abraham came and received upon himself the reward of them all.

5:20.en: Judah son of Tema says: Be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle, swift as a deer, and strong as a lion, to do the will of your Father in Heaven. He used to say: The bold-faced to Gehinnom, and the shamefaced to the Garden of Eden. May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You rebuild Your city speedily in our days, and give us our portion in Your Torah.

5:21.en: He used to say: At five years old, for Scripture; at ten, for Mishnah; at thirteen, for the commandments; at fifteen, for Talmud; at eighteen, for the wedding canopy; at twenty, for pursuit; at thirty, for strength; at forty, for understanding; at fifty, for counsel; at sixty, for old age; at seventy, for gray hair; at eighty, for might; at ninety, for stooping; at a hundred, it is as if he had died and passed away and ceased from the world.

5:22.en: Ben Bag Bag says: Turn it and turn it, for everything is in it; and in it you will see, and grow old and worn in it, and do not move from it, for you have no quality better than it.

5:23.en: Ben He He says: According to the toil is the reward.

5:3.en: Abraham our father, peace be upon him, was tested with ten trials and stood firm in all of them, to make known how great was the love of Abraham our father, peace be upon him.

5:4.en: Ten miracles were done for our fathers in Egypt, and ten at the sea. Ten plagues the Holy One, blessed be He, brought upon the Egyptians in Egypt, and ten at the sea. With ten trials our fathers tested the Omnipresent, blessed be He, in the wilderness, as it is said (Numbers 14): "They have tested me these ten times, and have not listened to my voice."

5:5.en: Ten miracles were done for our fathers in the Temple. No woman miscarried from the smell of the holy flesh; and the holy flesh never turned putrid; and no fly was seen in the slaughterhouse; and no emission befell the high priest on the Day of Atonement; and the rains did not extinguish the fire of the wood-pile; and the wind did not overcome the column of smoke; and no disqualification was found in the omer, the two loaves, or the showbread; they stood pressed together and bowed with room to spare; and no serpent or scorpion ever harmed anyone in Jerusalem; and no man said to his fellow, "The place is too narrow for me to lodge in Jerusalem."

5:6.en: Ten things were created on the eve of the Sabbath at twilight, and these are they: the mouth of the earth, the mouth of the well, the mouth of the donkey, the rainbow, the manna, the staff, the shamir, the script, the inscription, and the tablets. And some say: also the demons, and the burial place of Moses, and the ram of Abraham our father. And some say: also tongs made with tongs.

5:7.en: Seven things are in the unformed person, and seven in the wise person. The wise person does not speak in the presence of one who is greater than he in wisdom and in number; does not break into his fellow's words; is not hasty to answer; asks to the point and answers according to the law; speaks to the first point first and to the last point last; says of what he has not heard, "I have not heard"; and admits the truth. And their opposites are in the unformed person.

5:8.en: Seven kinds of calamity come to the world for seven principal transgressions. When some of them tithe and some do not tithe, a famine of drought comes: some go hungry and some are sated. When they have resolved not to tithe, a famine of tumult and of drought comes. And for not taking the dough-offering, a famine of annihilation comes. Pestilence comes to the world for the death penalties stated in the Torah that were not delivered to the court, and for the produce of the seventh year. Sword comes to the world for the delaying of justice, for the perverting of justice, and for those who teach the Torah not according to the law.

5:9.en: A wild beast comes to the world for a vain oath and for the profanation of the Name. Exile comes to the world for those who worship idols, for forbidden sexual relations, for the shedding of blood, and for violating the release of the land. At four times pestilence increases: in the fourth year, in the seventh, at the close of the seventh year, and at the close of the festival in every single year. In the fourth, because of the poor man's tithe of the third. In the seventh, because of the poor man's tithe of the sixth. At the close of the seventh year, because of the produce of the seventh year. And at the close of the festival in every single year, because of the robbery of the gifts to the poor.

6:1.en: The sages taught in the language of the Mishnah; blessed is He who chose them and their teaching. Rabbi Meir says: Whoever engages in Torah for its own sake merits many things. Not only that, but the entire world is worthwhile for his sake. He is called friend, beloved, one who loves the Omnipresent, one who loves creatures, one who gladdens the Omnipresent, one who gladdens creatures. It clothes him in humility and awe, it fits him to be righteous, devout, upright and faithful, it keeps him far from sin and draws him near to merit. People derive from him the benefit of counsel and sound wisdom, understanding and strength, as it is said (Proverbs 8): "Mine are counsel and sound wisdom; I am understanding; mine is strength." It gives him kingship and dominion and the probing of judgment; the secrets of Torah are revealed to him; he becomes like a spring that grows ever stronger and like a river that never ceases; he is modest and patient, and he forgives insult done to him; it makes him great and raises him above all the works.

6:10.en: Five possessions the Holy One, blessed be He, acquired for Himself in His world, and these are they: Torah, one possession; heaven and earth, one possession; Abraham, one possession; Israel, one possession; the Temple, one possession. Torah: from where do we know it? For it is written: The LORD acquired me as the beginning of His way, before His works of old. Heaven and earth, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: Thus says the LORD: The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool; what house is it that you would build for Me and what is the place of My rest? And it says: How many are Your works, O LORD; You made them all in wisdom; the earth is full of Your possession. Abraham, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: And he blessed him and said: Blessed be Abram to God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth. Israel, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: Until Your people pass over, O LORD, until the people You acquired pass over. And it says: As for the holy ones who are in the land, they, and the majestic ones, all my delight is in them. The Temple, one possession: from where do we know it? For it is written: The place for Your dwelling You made, O LORD; the sanctuary, O LORD, Your hands established. And it says: And He brought them to the border of His holiness, this mountain that His right hand acquired.

6:11.en: Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world, He did not create it except for His glory, as it is said: Everyone who is called by My name and for My glory I created him, I formed him, indeed I made him. And it says: The LORD will reign forever and ever. Rabbi Hananya son of Akashya says: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to grant merit to Israel; therefore He gave them abundant Torah and commandments, as it is said: The LORD was pleased for the sake of His righteousness to magnify Torah and make it glorious.

6:2.en: Rabbi Joshua son of Levi said: Every single day a heavenly voice goes out from Mount Horeb, proclaiming and saying: Woe to the creatures for the insult done to the Torah! For whoever does not engage in Torah is called rebuked, as it is said (Proverbs 11): "A gold ring in a pig's snout: a beautiful woman who has turned from discretion." And it says (Exodus 32): "The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets." Do not read ḥarut (engraved) but ḥerut (freedom), for you have no free person except one who engages in the study of Torah. And whoever engages in the study of Torah, such a person is exalted, as it is said (Numbers 21): "And from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth."

6:3.en: One who learns from his fellow a single chapter, or a single halakhah, or a single verse, or a single saying, or even a single letter, must treat him with honor. For so we find with David, king of Israel, who learned from Ahithophel only two things, yet called him his teacher, his companion and his familiar, as it is said (Psalms 55): "And you, a man of my own rank, my companion and my familiar." Is this not an argument from the lesser to the greater? If David, king of Israel, who learned from Ahithophel only two things, called him his teacher, his companion and his familiar, then one who learns from his fellow a single chapter, or a single halakhah, or a single verse, or a single saying, or even a single letter, how much more so must he treat him with honor. And there is no honor but Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 3): "The wise shall inherit honor," and (Proverbs 28): "and the blameless shall inherit good"; and there is no good but Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 4): "For I have given you good teaching; do not forsake my Torah."

6:4.en: This is the way of Torah: you shall eat bread with salt, and drink water by measure, and sleep on the ground, and live a life of hardship, and toil in Torah. If you do this, (Psalms 128) "Happy are you, and it shall be well with you": happy are you in this world, and it shall be well with you in the world to come.

6:5.en: Do not seek greatness for yourself, and do not covet honor; do more than you learn. Do not crave the table of kings, for your table is greater than their table, and your crown is greater than their crown, and the master of your work is faithful to pay you the reward of your labor.

6:6.en: Torah is greater than the priesthood and than kingship, for kingship is acquired by thirty degrees, and the priesthood by twenty-four, but the Torah is acquired by forty-eight things. And these are they: by study, by hearing with the ear, by ordering the lips, by understanding of the heart, by discernment of the heart, by awe, by reverence, by humility, by joy, by purity, by serving the sages, by exact discussion with colleagues, and by the sharp debate of the students; by composure, by Scripture, by Mishnah; by little business, by little worldly occupation, by little pleasure, by little sleep, by little talk, by little laughter; by patience, by a good heart, by faith in the sages, and by accepting sufferings. One who knows his place, and who is glad in his portion, and who makes a fence around his words, and does not claim credit for himself; beloved, a lover of the Omnipresent, a lover of creatures, a lover of acts of righteousness, a lover of upright dealings, a lover of reproofs; who keeps far from honor, and does not puff up his heart over his learning, and does not take pleasure in giving rulings; who bears the yoke with his fellow, tips him toward the scale of merit, sets him on the truth, and sets him on peace; whose heart is settled in his study; who asks and answers, hears and adds; who learns in order to teach and who learns in order to practice; who makes his teacher wiser, and who sets what he has heard exactly right, and who says a thing in the name of the one who said it. Thus you have learned that whoever says a thing in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world, as it is said (Esther 2): "And Esther said to the king in the name of Mordecai."

6:7.en: Great is the Torah, in that it gives life to those who practice it in this world and in the world to come, as it is said: For they are life to those who find them, and healing to all his flesh. And it says: It shall be healing to your navel and refreshment to your bones. And it says: It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it, and those who support it are happy. And it says: For they are a wreath of grace for your head and necklaces for your throat. And it says: She will give to your head a wreath of grace; a crown of splendor she will present to you. And it says: For through me your days will increase, and years of life will be added to you. And it says: Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand, wealth and honor. And it says: For length of days and years of life and peace they will add to you. And it says: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.

6:8.en: Rabbi Shimon son of Yehudah, in the name of Rabbi Shimon son of Yochai, says: Beauty, strength, wealth, honor, wisdom, old age, gray hair, and children are fitting for the righteous and fitting for the world, as it is said: Gray hair is a crown of splendor; in the way of righteousness it is found. And it says: The splendor of young men is their strength, and the glory of the old is gray hair. And it says: The crown of the wise is their wealth. And it says: The crown of the old is children's children, and the splendor of children is their fathers. And it says: The moon will be abashed and the sun ashamed, for the LORD of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before His elders is glory. Rabbi Shimon son of Menasya says: These seven qualities that the sages enumerated for the righteous, all of them were fulfilled in Rabbi and in his sons.

6:9.en: Rabbi Yose son of Kisma said: Once I was walking on the road and a certain man met me, and he greeted me, and I returned his greeting. He said to me: Rabbi, from what place are you? I said to him: I am from a great city of sages and of scribes. He said to me: Rabbi, is it your wish to dwell with us in our place? And I will give you a thousand thousand dinars of gold and precious stones and pearls. I said to him: My son, if you give me all the silver and gold and precious stones and pearls that are in the world, I dwell nowhere except in a place of Torah. And not only that, but at the hour of a person's departure nothing accompanies a person: neither silver nor gold nor precious stones or pearls, but only Torah and good deeds, as it is said: When you walk, it will lead you; when you lie down, it will watch over you; and when you awake, it will talk with you. When you walk, it will lead you in this world; when you lie down, it will watch over you in the grave; and when you awake, it will talk with you in the world to come. And so it is written in the Book of Psalms by the hand of David, king of Israel: The Torah of Your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver. And it says: Mine is the silver and mine is the gold, says the LORD of hosts.
